newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary allocates HUF 300 mln for small exporters.
newsitem.headline: Hungary allocates HUF 300 mln for small exporters.

text.p: Hungary said on Wednesday a preferential 300 million forint ($1.7 million) export financing scheme will generate some seven to eight billion forints of additional exports from small- and medium-sized firms.

"Our goal is to create a healthy export structure with numerous small companies at the base and a few giants at the top," Industry and Trade Minister Szabolcs Fazakas told journalists after signing this year's agreement with state-owned Eximbank.
Eximbank was created with the primary aim of providing preferential export financing not available through commercial banks, Fazakas said.
Last year, the bank financed 49 export deals, of which only one turned out to be a bad debt, a bank official said.
"The 200 million forints available in 1996 made possible exports of some 4.5 billion forints," said Eximabnk General Manager Ivan Nyiri.

He added that the bank, set up in 1994, now has sufficient expertise to handle the 300 million forints export loan subsidy available. Last year, it only undertook to manage 200 million forints out of the available 800 million.
Nyiri also said Eximbank's financing had been directed towards encouraging increased trade with former communist countries.
"Last year, we financed our first export deals towards Slovakia, Romania, Russia, the Ukraine and Yugoslavia," he said.

This year, preferential loans of up to 100 million forints worth of foreign currencies are available to domestic companies with maximum 1996 turnover of 2.5 billion forints and less than 250 employees.
The maximum loan period is six months, with an interest rate of 2 percentage points over LIBOR, half of it subsidised by the state.
According to customs statistics, Hungary's exports grew to $16 billion in 1996 from $12.9 billion in 1995, while the trade deficit widened to $2.7 billion in 1996 from $2.6 billion the year before.
-- Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040 ($ = 177.2 Hungarian Forints)
